handoff: Changes requested: the cli integration test's wait loops (until(() => true)) never tick, so the spec-folder-only check and AC3's waiting at merge are never observed. Core guard and validation meet AC1–AC2; unit tier and typecheck green.

findings.title: The integration tests' waiting loops run no ticks, so 'keeps waiting' and 'waits at merge' are never observed
findings.detail:
`until(done, max)` loops `for (i = 0; i < max && !done(); i++)`, so `until(() => true)` returns at once without a tick. The AC2 test 'a spec-folder-only change stays local; the story keeps waiting at merge' (line 227: `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) await until(() => true)`) commits `notes.md` and then checks the state with no tick in between: it passes even if observe or decide would bounce a spec-folder-only change to open-pr. The AC3 test (line 217) is the same: after `until(at("merge"))` it runs no tick at merge, so a push made while the story waits at merge would not show in `branchPushes()`. AC2: 'spec-folder-only differences stay local and the story keeps waiting'. AC3: 'waits at the merge step, then the PR's head on the remote is the commit ci watched: no story branch push happened after ci passed or ready approved'. The third test's receipt detail (only `fix.txt`) shows the filtering indirectly, but neither test proves what it claims.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Run real ticks in both places, e.g. a helper `async function ticks(n) { for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { h.clock.advance(10_000); hostSeesBranch(); await h.tick("--sync"); } }`, and use it on lines 217 and 227. Then check the AC2 test fails if the spec-folder filter in `unpushedCode` (packages/core/src/decide/story.ts:333) is removed.

findings.title: The guard covers merge-bound gates only, a narrower reading of 'a gate'
findings.detail:
AC1 and AC2 say 'a gate or a merge step'. `mergeBoundSteps` limits both the static rule and the runtime guard to merge steps and to gates with a path to merge or $done that avoids open-pr (ready, merge). It excludes human-qa and approve-slices. The handoff gives the reason: the literal reading would refuse the shipped story workflow, which AC1 says must validate. The reading is consistent and follows the slice Goal. It is still a scope decision the person should confirm.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: No change needed if the person accepts the reading. Cite it in the PR body.
